Overview

Nairobi as a Business Centre

Nairobi is the capital of Kenya and the principal financial and commercial centre of East Africa. The 2019 census counted about 4.4 million residents in Nairobi City County, and the county alone generated 27.5 percent of Kenya's GDP according to 2022 national statistics, with the wider metropolitan region producing around 40 percent. The Nairobi Securities Exchange, one of Africa's oldest, lists the country's leading banks, insurers and telecoms groups, including Safaricom. Multinationals have long used Nairobi as their African or East African headquarters, and the United Nations Office at Nairobi hosts the global headquarters of UN Environment and UN-Habitat, giving the city a substantial diplomatic and development community.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Nairobi because it is where regional decisions, contracts and money tend to concentrate. Investors and lenders need reliable background on Kenyan groups whose ownership runs through family holdings, trusts or offshore vehicles. Multinationals with regional offices in Upper Hill or Westlands face procurement fraud, conflicts of interest and distributor disputes that extend into neighbouring markets. The city's fintech and mobile money sector raises questions about partners, agents and payment flows. Development funders and NGOs need integrity checks on implementing partners. Counsel in Nairobi litigation and arbitration need well-sourced facts about counterparties and their assets.

Typical Matters

Investigative Work Connected to Nairobi

01

Regional headquarters internal investigations

Supporting counsel investigating suspected kickbacks, inflated supplier invoices or conflicts of interest at a Nairobi regional office, with background research on vendors, agents and intermediaries across East Africa and careful scoping of employee data under Kenya's data protection rules.

02

Fintech and payments partner diligence

Background research on Nairobi payment, lending and mobile money businesses and their founders before partnerships, investments or licensing arrangements, covering ownership, litigation, regulatory notices and media history, so clients understand who controls customer funds and where conduct or fraud risk sits.

03

Public procurement and contractor integrity

Research on contractors and consultants bidding for national or county government work in Nairobi, testing ownership links to officials, prior debarments or disputes, and company age and capacity, to support compliance reviews by lenders, joint venture partners and development funders.

04

Family group and ownership mapping

Tracing the ownership of Kenyan conglomerates, real estate developers and holding companies whose interests run through family members, nominees, trusts or offshore vehicles, using company searches, court records, gazette notices and foreign registries to identify the people who make decisions.

05

Dispute and asset research for counsel

Assembling factual records for counsel in commercial litigation or arbitration seated in Nairobi, including counterparties' related companies, prior judgments, published charges and land interests, and publicly reported assets relevant to security, injunctions and enforcement of awards or foreign judgments.

Local Context

Courts, Records and Institutions in Nairobi

Nairobi courts

Nairobi hosts the Supreme Court, the Court of Appeal and the High Court's principal stations, including its commercial and tax work, alongside the Environment and Land Court and the Employment and Labour Relations Court. The Nairobi Law Courts stand on City Square in the central business district. Published decisions on Kenya Law are an important source on a counterparty's dispute and insolvency history, although unreported matters and pending files require counsel's assistance to review.

Nairobi Centre for International Arbitration

The Nairobi Centre for International Arbitration was created by statute in 2013 to promote international commercial arbitration and other forms of alternative dispute resolution. The Act also established an Arbitral Court with a President, Deputy President and up to fifteen leading arbitrators. In April 2026 the Prime Cabinet Secretary and the Chief Justice publicly called for reforms to make the centre more independent of government, and an Arbitration (Amendment) Bill 2025 proposes limits on court intervention.

International organisations and development

The United Nations Office at Nairobi is one of the UN's four major duty stations outside headquarters and hosts the global headquarters of UN Environment and UN-Habitat. Many development finance institutions, foundations and NGOs run regional programmes from the city. That concentration creates demand for integrity due diligence on implementing partners, grantees and suppliers, and for careful handling of allegations involving staff covered by privileges and immunities.

Business districts and regional headquarters

Corporate activity has spread from the central business district to Upper Hill and Westlands, each about four kilometres away, where banks, professional firms and regional offices of global companies cluster. Several multinationals moved their African headquarters to Nairobi from 2007 onward. For investigations, this means that many East African contracts, approvals and payment decisions are taken in Nairobi even when the operations sit in Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ethiopia or South Sudan.

Engagement Standard

How TDSC Scopes Matters in Nairobi

For matters touching Nairobi, TDSC starts by defining the decision the client faces and which Kenyan and regional records can lawfully inform it. Research is carried out from Nashville using Business Registration Service company records, Kenya Law judgments, gazette notices, Nairobi Securities Exchange disclosures, regulator notices and local media in English and Kiswahili. Because many Nairobi matters reach into neighbouring countries, scoping identifies early which other registries and languages are needed. Where field enquiries, discreet interviews or document retrieval are justified, TDSC coordinates with appropriately licensed Kenyan professionals and the client's Kenyan counsel. Personal data is limited to what the purpose requires and handled consistently with Kenya's data protection law.

TDSC has no office in Nairobi. Engagements are directed from Nashville, Tennessee; where work on the ground is needed, it is performed by appropriately licensed local professionals under a written scope.

Questions

Nairobi: Frequently Asked Questions

Can you check whether a Nairobi company's owners are connected to public officials?

We research shareholders, directors and their known associates through company records, gazette notices, court decisions, procurement publications and media archives, and compare them with public information on officials and their families. We report connections that are documented and say clearly where links are only suggested. We do not access restricted government databases or the closed beneficial ownership register.

Do you support investigations at a regional office in Nairobi that covers several countries?

Yes. We help counsel scope the inquiry across each country involved, research vendors and intermediaries in those markets, and plan any interviews or document collection with local counsel. Personal data on Kenyan employees is handled in line with Kenya's data protection law, and the cross-border reach of the work is mapped before collection begins.

How useful is arbitration in Nairobi for enforcing against a Kenyan counterparty?

That is a legal question for counsel, but we can supply the facts that shape it: where the counterparty holds assets, which related companies might be involved, its record of complying with or resisting prior judgments and awards, and any insolvency proceedings. Nairobi's arbitration framework is under reform discussion in 2026, so counsel should confirm the current position.

Can you vet NGO or development partners based in Nairobi?

We conduct integrity due diligence on implementing partners, grantees and suppliers, covering registration, governance, leadership backgrounds, litigation, sanctions and adverse media. Where allegations concern staff of international organisations, we work through the client's counsel and internal oversight function, since privileges and immunities may affect what can be done and by whom.

Does TDSC have an office in Nairobi?

No. TDSC is based in Nashville and has no office, staff or address in Nairobi or elsewhere in Kenya. Most work is desk-based research. Where on-the-ground steps are needed, we coordinate with appropriately licensed Kenyan professionals acting lawfully alongside the client's counsel, and we decline requests involving restricted records or unlawful methods.
